- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.5) in recent days, reduce forecast slope or shift downward by 2–5% to account for bearish momentum.  
- If forecast is rising steadily (e.g., +0.5–1.0% per day) and sentiment is neutral or positive, check for over-optimism — cap upward trend at 1–2% above recent 7-day average.  
- After a sharp spike in price (e.g., +10%+ in 3–5 days), model often overcorrects — reduce forecast by 3–8% in next 5–7 days to avoid overshoot.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 50% of 30d moving avg), model tends to lag — adjust forecast to align with 10–15 day moving avg.  
- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.5) and forecast is flat or declining, model underestimates rebound — increase forecast by 1–3% per day for next 3–5 days.  
- If true outcome deviates >10% from forecast in first 3 days, reset forecast to 30d moving avg and re-estimate slope based on sentiment trend.  
- Avoid forecasting beyond 10% above recent 30d high — sentiment-driven corrections often occur within 3–5 days after peak.
